title: AITA for saying the word “girl” instead of “Woman” in conversation?
question: AITA for saying the word “girl” instead of “Woman” in conversation?
body:
This happened just last week.

I was talking with my manager (I’ll call her Steph) and another co-worker of ours (Let’s call him Brian). Brian was telling us about some of the great pro-bono work he had recently accomplished in helping recent immigrant refugees assimilate and succeed in America, through various events he puts on at work.

What I wanted to say next was- “I know a girl who has done similar work- and would want to get involved.” 

But all I was able to get out was- “I know a girl-“ because Steph interrupted me and says, “Woman.” 

It took me a few seconds to even comprehend what she was saying. I expected her to say something else, and I had to repeatedly ask her to clarify why she was saying the word “Woman,” before she finally said “You said girl, and the correct term is Woman.” 

To get over the awkwardness, I just changed the term and moved on- however since this has happened I’ve been really bothered about being forced to change my vocabulary. 

I didn’t use “girl” in a derogatory way, and if I was referencing a guy I wouldn’t have used the word “Man.” It also signaled to Brian that I was in the wrong, when I don’t feel as if I did anything wrong. I’ve experienced conversations where the word “woman” has had negative connotations in the past as well, so I feel as if I’m just playing catch-up to pander for whoever I’m speaking to by changing my word choice. 

Because of everything above, I’m not planning on changing my word choice in the future. Help me out reddit- AITA?
